guides.title: Fix "spawn npx ENOENT" for MCP servers on Windows
guides.seoTitle: Fix "spawn npx ENOENT" for MCP servers on Windows (the cmd /c fix)
guides.description: MCP server fails on Windows with spawn npx ENOENT or Connection closed? Wrap npx in cmd /c. Exact config for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and Codex, plus other causes.
guides.markdown:
You add a local MCP server that starts with `npx`, it works on a Mac, and on Windows your AI client reports `spawn npx ENOENT` (or a vague "Connection closed" or "Failed to connect"). This is a well-known Windows quirk, and the usual fix is a three-word change to your config. This guide explains why it happens, gives the exact fix for each client, and lists the other causes to rule out.

## Quick answer

1. In your MCP config, change `"command": "npx"` to `"command": "cmd"`.
2. Put `"/c"` and `"npx"` at the start of `args`, before the rest of the arguments.
3. Save, then fully quit and reopen your client (not just a new chat).

_Only the command and the first two args change_

```json
// before: fails on Windows in some clients
{
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
}

// after
{
  "command": "cmd",
  "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
}
```

Not every client needs this. The official MCP quickstart for Claude Desktop uses plain `npx` on Windows, and if your server already connects you should leave it alone. Use the wrapper when you see the error.

## Why it happens

`ENOENT` means "no such file": the program that started your MCP server could not find the command you gave it. On Windows, `npx` is not a program (`npx.exe`) but a script launcher called `npx.cmd`. Many MCP clients start servers directly, with no shell in between, and a directly-started process cannot resolve `npx` to `npx.cmd`. Node's own documentation says that `.bat` and `.cmd` files are not executable on their own without a terminal and can only be run through `cmd.exe` (or by spawning with a shell).

You also cannot fix it by pointing at `npx.cmd`. Since the April 2024 Node.js security releases (CVE-2024-27980), starting a `.cmd` or `.bat` file without a shell fails with `EINVAL` on Node 18.20.2, 20.12.2 and later. So the reliable route is to start `cmd.exe` yourself, and let it run `npx`: `cmd /c npx ...`. `/c` tells `cmd` to run the rest as a command and exit.

The MCP server READMEs use this pattern for Windows. The official Filesystem server README, for instance, has a Windows config that starts with `"command": "cmd"` and `"/c", "npx"`. Users reported the same fix in Claude Code issue #3369, where a native-Windows setup showed `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` until the config was changed to `cmd /c`. A reply there said the `cmd` solutions fix it.

## The fix, per client

Every client uses the same idea: `command` is `cmd`, and `args` begins with `/c` and `npx`. Each argument stays a separate string. The server here is the official [Memory server](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/memory-mcp/); swap in your own package and arguments.

### Claude Code

With the CLI, everything after `--` is the command. Keep each word separate (do not wrap the whole command in one pair of quotes) and keep the `--`:

_Run in PowerShell or Command Prompt_

```bash
claude mcp add memory -- cmd /c npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
```

To change an existing entry, remove it first (`claude mcp remove memory`) and add it again. Or add it from JSON, which keeps the arguments exactly as you write them:

_Bash or Git Bash quoting. In PowerShell, escape the inner quotes or put the JSON in a .mcp.json file instead_

```bash
claude mcp add-json memory '{"type":"stdio","command":"cmd","args":["/c","npx","-y","@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]}'
```

In a project `.mcp.json` file at the repository root, use the same `command` and `args` shape under `mcpServers`. Check the result with `claude mcp get memory`, which prints the command Claude Code will run, and `claude mcp list`.

A note on versions: Claude Code's current MCP docs say that executables on your `PATH` such as `npx` or `uvx` work as-is, and do not mention `cmd /c`. Users on native Windows have reported otherwise in issues #3369, #9594 and #68221 (the last one traces it to the `EINVAL` behaviour above). Some Claude Code versions have printed a warning that a Windows `npx` server needs the `cmd /c` wrapper. If plain `npx` connects for you, you do not need the wrapper.

### Claude Desktop

Open the config from **Settings**, then **Developer**, then **Edit Config**. The file is `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows.

_%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json_

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

Save the file, then completely quit Claude Desktop and reopen it; the MCP docs say it must restart to load the new configuration.

### Cursor

Same shape in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (project). More in [how to add an MCP server to Cursor](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/add-mcp-server-to-cursor/), which also shows this wrapper in its troubleshooting section.

_~/.cursor/mcp.json_

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

VS Code uses a `servers` key (not `mcpServers`) in `.vscode/mcp.json` for a workspace, or in your user profile's `mcp.json`. Open either from the Command Palette with **MCP: Open Workspace Folder MCP Configuration** or **MCP: Open User Configuration**.

_.vscode/mcp.json_

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "memory": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

Update Codex first. A fix merged on 16 November 2025 (pull request #3828, "resolve Windows MCP server execution for script-based tools") makes Codex resolve script launchers such as `npx`, `pnpm` and `yarn` through the Windows `PATHEXT` list, so a recent Codex may need no wrapper at all. If you still get the error on a current build, use the same shape in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

_~/.codex/config.toml (%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml on Windows)_

```text
[mcp_servers.memory]
command = "cmd"
args = ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
```

Older Codex versions behaved differently. A 2025 issue on Codex 0.23 (#2555) reports `cmd /c` timing out with "request timed out", and another (#3385) describes using the full path to `npx.cmd` together with a larger `startup_timeout_sec`. Those are user reports against old releases, so try updating before using them. Full config details are in [how to add an MCP server to Codex](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/add-mcp-server-to-codex-config-toml/).

## If it still fails: other causes

### Node.js is not installed, or the client cannot see it

Open a new Command Prompt and run `where node` and `where npx`. If either prints nothing, install Node.js. If they work in your terminal but not in the client, the client was started before Node was on your PATH: quit it fully and reopen it, or sign out and back in.

### The server runs fine by hand

Run the full command yourself, for example `cmd /c npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`. A working MCP server starts and then waits silently for input (press Ctrl+C to stop it). If it prints an error and returns to the prompt, fix that error first; the client is only reporting it. Official servers need Node 24 or newer from v2 onward (see [what changed in v2](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/mcp-reference-servers-v2-whats-changed/)).

### `${APPDATA}` or npm folder errors (Claude Desktop)

The MCP docs describe an `ENOENT` where the server log mentions `${APPDATA}` in a path. The fix they give is to add the expanded value to the server's `env`, for example `"APPDATA": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Roaming\\"`, and to make sure npm is installed globally, so that `%APPDATA%\npm` exists (`npm install -g npm` creates it).

### The command is not an `.cmd` script at all

The wrapper is for launchers that are `.cmd` or `.bat` scripts, such as `npx`, `npm`, `pnpm` and `yarn`. A real `.exe` such as `node.exe` does not need it. Use an absolute path for your own scripts, since a relative one resolves against whatever folder the client was started from.

### Backslashes in JSON

In JSON, a Windows path needs doubled backslashes, `C:\\Users\\you\\projects`, or forward slashes. A single backslash makes the file invalid or changes the path. In Codex's TOML file use single-quoted strings, `'C:\Users\you\projects'`, which TOML treats literally.

Still seeing "Connection closed"? That message covers many causes; work through [Fix MCP error -32000 "Connection closed"](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-mcp-error-32000-connection-closed/).

## FAQ

### Does this apply to WSL?

The cause is specific to launching `.cmd` scripts from native Windows. Inside WSL you run Linux versions of the tools, where `npx` is a normal executable. The issue above notes that the same setup worked in WSL2.

### Do I need `cmd /c` for `uvx` or Python servers?

Not for the same reason. `npx`, `npm`, `pnpm` and `yarn` are the `.cmd` launchers. A server started with `uvx` or `python` is a different command, so only wrap it if you see an equivalent error.

### Why not just use the full path to npx.cmd?

Since the CVE-2024-27980 hardening, Node refuses to start a `.cmd` file without a shell, and the failure is `EINVAL` rather than `ENOENT`. Going through `cmd /c` avoids the problem.

guides.title: Fix MCP error -32000: "Connection closed"
guides.seoTitle: Fix MCP error -32000 "Connection closed" (causes and fixes)
guides.description: MCP error -32000 "Connection closed" means your MCP server process exited or never started. How to find the real cause with a 60-second test, the common fixes, and where each client keeps its logs.
guides.markdown:
You add an MCP server, restart your client, and get `MCP error -32000: Connection closed`. The message is accurate but unhelpful: it only says that the connection to the server ended. The cause is almost always on the server side, usually in the first second after it launches. This guide shows how to find it fast.

## Quick answer

`-32000` is the code the MCP SDKs use for `ConnectionClosed`. For a local (stdio) server it means the server process exited, or its pipe closed, before the client finished talking to it. So the job is to find out why the server stopped:

1. Copy the exact `command`, `args` and `env` from your config and run that command yourself in a terminal.
2. Read what it prints. A healthy stdio server starts and then waits silently for input. If it prints an error and returns to the prompt, that error is your answer (wrong Node version, missing package, missing API key, bad path).
3. Fix that, then restart the client fully. If you are on Windows and the command starts with `npx`, try the [`cmd /c` fix](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-spawn-npx-enoent-windows-mcp/) first.

The rest of this page covers the usual causes, where to find each client's logs, and how to test a server without any client.

## What the error means

MCP clients talk to a local server over its standard input and output. When the process behind that pipe ends, the SDK rejects every pending request with `MCP error -32000: Connection closed`. We reproduced it with the official TypeScript SDK: a server command that starts and then exits with an error code produces exactly that message. A command that does not exist at all produces a different one, a `spawn ... ENOENT` error, because the client could not even start the process.

The error comes from the client, not the server, so the same server can show it in Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and Codex. What differs between clients is only where the useful detail is logged.

## Step 1: run the server by hand

This is the same test the Claude Code docs recommend. Run the server's command exactly as written in your config, with the same environment variables:

```bash
# example: the official Memory server
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
```

- **It starts and sits there:** the server itself works (press Ctrl+C to stop it). The problem is how the client launches it: the path, the environment, the working directory, or Windows `npx` (next section).
- **It prints an error and exits:** the message names what is missing, such as a Node.js version, a package, or an environment variable. That is the real cause.

Set any `env` values from your config in the same terminal first (for example `export API_KEY=...` on macOS and Linux, or `$env:API_KEY = "..."` in PowerShell).

## Step 2: the common causes

### Windows and `npx`

On native Windows, a client that launches `npx` directly can fail to start it. One of the first reports of this exact `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` was Claude Code issue #3369 on native Windows. Wrap the command in `cmd /c`: see [Fix "spawn npx ENOENT" for MCP servers on Windows](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-spawn-npx-enoent-windows-mcp/).

### The runtime is missing or too old

The server needs Node.js, Python or uv, and the client cannot find it or finds an old copy. Check `node --version` in the same environment the client uses. The official TypeScript reference servers declare Node 24 or newer from v2.0.0 (see [what changed in the MCP reference servers v2](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/mcp-reference-servers-v2-whats-changed/)), and a server that needs `uvx` needs uv installed. After installing a runtime, quit and reopen the client so it sees the new PATH.

### A required API key or setting is missing

Many servers exit immediately if a required environment variable is not set. Check the server's README for its variables, and set them in the config's `env` block, not only in your shell. Claude Code's troubleshooting notes that a server may miss variables that are not in its own config entry, because the client passes a limited environment to stdio servers.

### A wrong or relative path

Use absolute paths for local scripts and folders. Claude Code's docs say relative paths in `command` or `args` are a frequent cause of failed starts, because they resolve against the folder you launched the client from, not the config file's folder. Programs on your PATH, such as `npx` or `uvx`, are fine as they are.

### The command was added wrongly (Claude Code)

With `claude mcp add`, everything after the `--` separator is the server command. If you leave out the `--`, or quote the whole command as one string, Claude Code parses the pieces wrongly. Run `claude mcp get <name>` and check that the command shown is what you intended; if not, `claude mcp remove <name>` and add it again.

### The package cannot be downloaded

The first `npx -y` run downloads the package, which can fail on an offline machine, behind a proxy, or with a broken npm cache. Running the command by hand (Step 1) shows the npm error. A slow first download can instead end as a startup timeout; Claude Code's default is 30 seconds and can be raised with `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000 claude`, and Codex's default is 10 seconds, raised with `startup_timeout_sec` in `config.toml`.

### The server crashes on startup, or writes to stdout

If you wrote the server yourself, remember that a stdio server must never print logs to standard output: the MCP docs warn that it corrupts the JSON-RPC messages and breaks the server. Use stderr (`console.error` in Node, the `logging` module in Python). A plain crash on startup, such as an import error, also ends the connection.

## Step 3: read the client's logs

- **Claude Desktop:** logs are in `~/Library/Logs/Claude` on macOS and `%APPDATA%\Claude\logs` on Windows. `mcp.log` covers connections and failures, and `mcp-server-<name>.log` holds that server's stderr output.
- **Claude Code:** run `/mcp` to see which server failed. `claude mcp list` and `claude mcp get <name>` show failure details. For a server's stderr, run `claude --debug=mcp` and read the log under `~/.claude/debug/`.
- **Cursor:** open the Output panel (Cmd+Shift+U on Mac, Ctrl+Shift+U on Windows and Linux) and choose **MCP Logs**. See [how to add an MCP server to Cursor](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/add-mcp-server-to-cursor/).
- **VS Code:** run **MCP: List Servers** from the Command Palette, pick the server, and choose to show its output.
- **Codex:** run `codex mcp list` to check the entry, and type `/mcp` in the terminal UI to see active servers.

## Step 4: test the server without a client

The [MCP Inspector](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/mcp-inspector/) runs your server and lets you list and call its tools in a browser, with the client taken out of the picture. If the server works there, the problem is your client config; if it fails there too, the server is the problem.

_Inspector, then your server's command and arguments (this example launches a locally built Node server)_

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node build/index.js
```

## FAQ

### Is -32000 always a local server problem?

The code means "connection closed", which can also happen with a remote server if the connection drops. The advice above is for local stdio servers, which is where this error shows up most. For a remote server that needs sign-in, see [Claude Code MCP "needs authentication"](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-claude-code-mcp-needs-authentication/).

### It worked yesterday. What changed?

Usually the runtime or the package. With `npx -y` and no version, npx fetches the latest release on each launch, so a server update (or a Node update on your machine) can change behaviour. The official reference servers moved to v2 in October 2026; pinning a version with `package@version` is a quick way to test.

### Does a stdout log line cause this error?

The MCP docs say writing to stdout from a stdio server corrupts the protocol and breaks the server. We could not show that a stray stdout line by itself produces `-32000` in our own test, so treat it as a likely cause for a custom server and rely on Step 1 to confirm it.

guides.title: Fix Claude Code MCP "needs authentication"
guides.seoTitle: Fix Claude Code MCP "needs authentication" (sign in with /mcp)
guides.description: A remote MCP server shows "Needs authentication" in Claude Code? Sign in from /mcp or with claude mcp login, then fix expired tokens, headless sessions and servers that need a fixed callback port.
guides.markdown:
You added a remote MCP server to Claude Code and `claude mcp list` shows `! Needs authentication`, or a tool call fails and asks you to sign in again. That is not a broken install: Claude Code connected, the server answered 401 or 403, and it is waiting for you to log in. Here is how to finish the sign-in and what to check when it will not stick.

## Quick answer

1. Start Claude Code and run `/mcp`.
2. Select the server that needs authentication and follow the steps in the browser window that opens to log in and approve access.
3. Run `claude mcp list` (or `/mcp` again) and check the server now shows `✔ Connected`.

Prefer the terminal, or working over SSH? Run `claude mcp login <name>` instead (add `--no-browser` to get a URL you can open on another machine and paste the redirect URL back). To sign out later, run `claude mcp logout <name>`.

## Why you see it

Claude Code marks a remote server as needing authentication when the server responds with `401 Unauthorized` or `403 Forbidden`, so you can complete the OAuth flow. OAuth in Claude Code applies to remote HTTP servers. A local stdio server does not use it; those take keys through environment variables (`claude mcp add --env KEY=value ...`), and a failing one is a different problem, covered in [Fix MCP error -32000](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-mcp-error-32000-connection-closed/).

Claude Code stores the tokens it gets and refreshes them automatically. If a stored token is rejected, it refreshes and retries once before it flags the server again, so a flag that keeps returning usually means the refresh token was revoked or expired.

## Add a server that needs sign-in, then authenticate

The example from the Claude Code docs adds Sentry's remote server. See also the [Sentry MCP listing](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/sentry-mcp/) and the [Notion](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/notion-mcp/) and [Linear](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/linear-mcp/) servers, which use the same flow.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
claude
# then inside Claude Code:
/mcp
```

If you already added the server, running `claude mcp add` again with the same name at the same scope fails with a message that the server already exists. Skip straight to `/mcp`.

More on adding servers to Claude Code is in [the best MCP servers for Claude Code](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/best-mcp-servers-for-claude-code/).

## If sign-in does not complete

### The browser does not open, or the redirect fails

- If the browser does not open on its own, copy the URL Claude Code shows and open it manually.
- If the redirect shows a connection error after you approve access, copy the full callback URL from your browser's address bar and paste it into the URL prompt that Claude Code shows.
- Over SSH, or on Linux with no display, `claude mcp login <name>` detects there is no local browser and prints the URL instead. Open it on your own machine and paste the redirect URL back. It needs an interactive terminal for that paste step.

### "MCP server needs you to sign in again"

The full message in the Claude Code docs is `MCP server "<name>" needs you to sign in again (run /mcp to re-authenticate)`. It means a sign-in expired or was revoked, or the token lacks a permission the tool needs. Run `/mcp`, select the server, and choose **Re-authenticate**. If the same error returns for one specific tool, the token may be missing a scope; Claude Code requests the scopes pinned in the server's config (`oauth.scopes`) when they are set, so add the missing scope there before signing in again.

### You use claude -p or the Agent SDK

Headless runs have no `/mcp` panel, so Claude Code cannot run the OAuth flow there. Sign in once from an interactive session (`/mcp`, or `claude mcp login <name>` in your shell), then start the run again.

### You set an Authorization header yourself

If the server entry has `headers.Authorization` (or a `headersHelper`) and the server rejects it, Claude Code reports the connection as failed rather than falling back to OAuth. Fix the token, or remove the header to use the OAuth flow. If the header comes from a `${VAR}`, check that the variable is set; Claude Code warns about unset ones in `claude mcp list` and `/mcp`.

### The server requires a pre-registered redirect URI or client

By default Claude Code uses a random free port for the OAuth callback. Servers that only accept a redirect URI of the form `http://localhost:PORT/callback` registered in advance need a fixed port, and some need a pre-registered client ID:

_Replace the name, URL and ID with your server's_

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --callback-port 8080 my-server https://mcp.example.com/mcp

# with a pre-registered OAuth client (the secret is prompted for, masked)
claude mcp add --transport http --client-id your-client-id --client-secret --callback-port 8080 my-server https://mcp.example.com/mcp
```

### The same server name is defined in two scopes

Claude Code stores OAuth sign-ins per endpoint. If one name points at different URLs in different scopes (for example a user-level and a project-level entry), signing in to one does not sign you in to the other, and `claude mcp list` warns about the conflict. Keep one definition and remove the rest with `claude mcp remove`.

### Google, Microsoft 365 and other Anthropic-hosted connectors

Some Anthropic-hosted connectors, such as Gmail, Google Calendar and Microsoft 365, do not support local OAuth from Claude Code, because the identity provider only accepts the redirect URL registered by claude.ai. If Claude Code says so, connect the service at claude.ai under **Customize**, then **Connectors**, and remove your own entry with `claude mcp remove <name>`; the connector then appears in Claude Code on its own.

### Start fresh

Choose **Clear authentication** from the server's menu in `/mcp`, or run `claude mcp logout <name>`, then authenticate again. If that still fails, `claude mcp remove <name>` and add the server again.

## FAQ

### Is "needs authentication" the same as "Failed to connect"?

No. `Failed to connect` means Claude Code could not reach or start the server, and `claude mcp get <name>` shows the HTTP status or error text. `Needs authentication` means it reached the server, and the server asked for credentials.

### Does a local server (npx, uvx) use /mcp to sign in?

No. OAuth sign-in is for remote HTTP servers. For a local server, put the API key in its environment with `--env` or the `env` block of `.mcp.json`.

### Can I do this for a team without everyone clicking through?

Each person signs in with their own account; tokens are stored per user. Teams can share the server definition through a project `.mcp.json` file, but not the credentials.

guides.title: How to add an MCP server to Codex
guides.seoTitle: How to add an MCP server to Codex (config.toml and codex mcp add)
guides.description: Add an MCP server to OpenAI Codex with codex mcp add or config.toml: file locations, stdio and remote examples, env vars, timeouts, OAuth login and fixes for common errors.
guides.markdown:
Codex (the CLI, the IDE extension and the desktop app) can use MCP servers to reach tools and data beyond your repository. You add one either with a single `codex mcp add` command or by editing `config.toml`, and all Codex surfaces share the same configuration. This guide covers both, with examples built from OpenAI's documentation.

## Quick answer

1. Run `codex mcp add <name> -- <command> <args>`. For example `codex mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp` (the example OpenAI's docs use).
2. Run `codex mcp list` to confirm it is saved.
3. Start `codex` and type `/mcp` to see the active servers.

The command writes a `[mcp_servers.<name>]` table into `~/.codex/config.toml`. You can edit that file directly for anything the command does not cover. The IDE extension and desktop app also have an **MCP servers** screen (in settings) that edits the same configuration.

## Where the config lives

- **Global:** `~/.codex/config.toml` (on Windows, in `.codex` under your user folder).
- **Project:** `.codex/config.toml` in a project, which Codex reads for trusted projects only.

The ChatGPT desktop app, the Codex CLI and the IDE extension share this configuration, so you set a server up once. ChatGPT on the web does not read your local Codex files; it uses plugins instead.

## Option 1: codex mcp add

_The general form from OpenAI's docs_

```bash
codex mcp add <server-name> --env VAR1=VALUE1 --env VAR2=VALUE2 -- <stdio server-command>
```

Everything after `--` is the command that starts the server. Put `--env` options before it. A few real examples, using servers listed on PluginStack:

```bash
# Context7: current library docs (example from the OpenAI docs)
codex mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp

# Official Memory server
codex mcp add memory -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory

# Official Filesystem server: the last argument is the folder it may access
codex mcp add filesystem -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /Users/you/projects
```

See [Context7](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/context7/), [Memory](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/memory-mcp/) and [Filesystem](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/filesystem-mcp/). The official TypeScript servers need Node 24 or newer from v2 onward ([what changed](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/mcp-reference-servers-v2-whats-changed/)).

### Other commands

- `codex mcp list` shows the configured servers.
- `codex mcp --help` lists all MCP commands.
- `codex mcp login <server-name>` starts the OAuth login for a server that supports it.

### A remote (HTTP) server

For a hosted server, pass its address with `--url` instead of a command:

_Then run: codex mcp login example (if the server uses OAuth)_

```bash
codex mcp add example --url https://mcp.example.com
```

## Option 2: edit config.toml

Each server is a `[mcp_servers.<name>]` table. For a local (stdio) server, `command` is required; `args`, `env`, `env_vars` and `cwd` are optional:

_~/.codex/config.toml_

```text
[mcp_servers.filesystem]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/Users/you/projects"]

[mcp_servers.context7]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]
startup_timeout_sec = 20   # default is 10
```

The table name (`filesystem`) is the label you choose. Save the file and restart Codex (in the IDE extension, use **Restart extension**).

### Environment variables and API keys

- `env` sets values for the server: `env = { API_KEY = "value" }`.
- `env_vars` lists variable names to allow and forward from your own environment, such as `env_vars = ["API_KEY"]`, so the secret does not have to sit in the file.

Prefer `env_vars` for real keys, and never commit a `config.toml` that contains one. A project-level `.codex/config.toml` is easy to commit by accident.

### A remote server in config.toml

```text
[mcp_servers.example]
url = "https://mcp.example.com"
bearer_token_env_var = "EXAMPLE_TOKEN"   # token read from this variable, sent in Authorization
```

For HTTP servers, `url` is required. You can add a bearer token from an environment variable (`bearer_token_env_var`), static headers (`http_headers`), or headers read from variables (`env_http_headers`). With none of those, Codex tries stored OAuth credentials, so run `codex mcp login <name>` for servers that use OAuth.

### Useful options

- `startup_timeout_sec`: seconds to wait for the server to start. Default 10. Raise it if the first `npx` download is slow.
- `tool_timeout_sec`: seconds a tool call may run. Default 60.
- `enabled = false`: switch a server off without deleting its config.
- `required = true`: make Codex fail at startup if that server cannot initialise.
- `enabled_tools` and `disabled_tools`: allow or deny specific tool names.
- `default_tools_approval_mode`: how Codex asks before running the server's tools (`auto`, `prompt`, `writes` or `approve`).

OpenAI's configuration reference has the complete list of MCP options. Settings change between Codex releases, so check it for your version.

## Check that it works

1. Run `codex mcp list`: the server should appear.
2. Start `codex` and type `/mcp`: the server should be listed as active.
3. Ask for something only that server can do, for example "Use the memory server to remember that I prefer tabs", and approve the tool call if asked.

## Common errors and fixes

- **The server does not appear:** check the table is `[mcp_servers.<name>]` (plural `mcp_servers`) and that the TOML is valid. For a project file, the project must be trusted.
- **It times out on the first run:** the first `npx -y` run downloads the package. Raise `startup_timeout_sec`, or run the command once by hand so it is cached.
- **`spawn npx ENOENT`, or it fails only on Windows:** update Codex, then see [Fix "spawn npx ENOENT" on Windows](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-spawn-npx-enoent-windows-mcp/).
- **The server exits at once:** run its command yourself in a terminal to see why. [Fix MCP error -32000](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/fix-mcp-error-32000-connection-closed/) walks through it.
- **An OAuth server stays unauthenticated:** run `codex mcp login <name>`; in the desktop app or IDE extension, use **Authenticate** in the MCP servers list.

Using Codex alongside other tools? The same servers can be added to [Cursor](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/add-mcp-server-to-cursor/) and [Claude Code](https://www.pluginstackai.com/guides/best-mcp-servers-for-claude-code/). More about the agent itself: [Codex CLI](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/codex-cli/).

## FAQ

### Is the config the same for the CLI and the IDE extension?

Yes. OpenAI's docs say the desktop app, CLI and IDE extension share MCP configuration, so you can switch between them without redoing setup.

### Where do I put an API key?

Use `env_vars` to forward a variable from your shell, or `bearer_token_env_var` for remote servers, so the key stays out of the file. If you use `env` or `codex mcp add --env`, the value is saved in `config.toml`; keep that file private.

### How do I turn a server off without removing it?

Set `enabled = false` in its `[mcp_servers.<name>]` table.

guides.title: Best free AI courses (2026)
guides.seoTitle: Best free AI courses (2026): beginner to builder
guides.description: Free AI courses for 2026, from no-code basics to building agents and MCP servers, each checked on its official page: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Hugging Face, fast.ai, CS50 and more.
guides.markdown:
You don't need to pay to learn AI. These are the best free courses we found, from total beginner (no coding) to building your own agents and MCP servers. For each one we say who it's for, what's actually free, and whether you get a certificate.

## Quick answer: where to start

- **Never used AI tools much?** Start with [Elements of AI](https://www.elementsofai.com/) or **Claude 101** from Anthropic Academy. No coding needed.
- **Want to use ChatGPT or Codex better at work?** [OpenAI Academy](https://academy.openai.com/).
- **Starting to code with AI?** **Claude Code 101** from Anthropic Academy, then our [Start here](https://www.pluginstackai.com/start-here/) page to set up your first tools.
- **Want to build agents?** The [Hugging Face Agents Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/agents-course/unit0/introduction) (basic Python needed).
- **Want to build MCP servers?** **Introduction to Model Context Protocol** from Anthropic Academy (Python).
- **Want the computer science behind it?** [Harvard CS50 AI](https://cs50.harvard.edu/ai/) or [fast.ai](https://course.fast.ai/).

> How we picked: the lessons have to be free to take. Where a certificate or extras cost money, we say so. We don't earn anything from these links.

## Beginner courses (no coding)

### OpenAI Academy

OpenAI's free, self-paced courses on using AI at work, building with AI and Codex, leading AI adoption, and teaching and learning with AI. You can browse without signing in, but you need a ChatGPT account to enroll and save your progress.

- **Cost:** free.
- **Certificate:** pass a course's assessment (80% or higher) to earn a shareable badge. Finish every course in a pathway (such as Foundations, Codex or API) for a certificate of completion. OpenAI says these are not formal certifications.
- **Link:** [academy.openai.com](https://academy.openai.com/)

### Anthropic Academy: Claude 101 and AI Fluency

Anthropic's free courses, hosted on Skilljar. (Anthropic's learning hub is now called [Claude Academy](https://academy.claude.com/); the course catalog is still headed Anthropic Academy.) Two good beginner picks:

- [Claude 101](https://anthropic.skilljar.com/claude-101): using Claude for everyday work, including projects, artifacts, skills and connecting your tools.
- [AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations](https://anthropic.skilljar.com/ai-fluency-framework-foundations): how to work with any AI effectively, efficiently, ethically and safely. Made with professors from University College Cork and Ringling College.
- **Cost:** free (you register for each course).
- **Certificate:** each course page lists a certificate of completion.

### Elements of AI

A free online course series from MinnaLearn and the University of Helsinki, taken by over 2 million people. **Introduction to AI** explains what AI is and what it can and can't do, with no complicated math or programming. **Building AI** is the follow-up and goes a step further (basic Python helps).

- **Cost:** free, self-paced.
- **Link:** [elementsofai.com](https://www.elementsofai.com/)

### Google: Introduction to Generative AI

A short (about 45 minutes) introductory course on what generative AI is, how it works and how it differs from traditional machine learning. It's on Google Skills (formerly Google Cloud Skills Boost) and you can earn a badge.

- **Cost:** free.
- **Link:** [Introduction to Generative AI on Google Skills](https://www.skills.google/course_templates/536)

> Heads up: **Google AI Essentials** is not free. Google says it costs $49 USD per month in the U.S. and Canada after a 7-day free trial (it may cost less in other countries). It's on Coursera. If you want a free Google option, take Introduction to Generative AI above.

## For people who code with AI

### Anthropic Academy: Claude Code 101

For developers who are new to software engineering, or experienced engineers who haven't tried AI coding agents yet. It goes from installing [Claude Code](https://www.pluginstackai.com/plugins/claude-code/) to customizing it for your daily work.

- **Cost:** free. (Using Claude Code itself needs a paid Claude plan or a Console account.)
- **Certificate:** certificate of completion.
- **Link:** [Claude Code 101](https://anthropic.skilljar.com/claude-code-101)

### DeepLearning.AI short courses

Short, hands-on courses on specific topics like prompting, agents, RAG and tools such as MCP, some made with the companies behind those tools (like Anthropic). A good way to learn one thing in an afternoon.

- **Cost:** the course videos are free to watch. Quizzes, labs and certificates of completion need a paid Pro membership.
- **Link:** [deeplearning.ai/courses](https://www.deeplearning.ai/courses)

## For people who want to build agents and models

### Anthropic Academy: Introduction to Model Context Protocol

Build MCP servers and clients from scratch in Python, covering MCP's three core parts: tools, resources and prompts. Take this after you've used a few MCP servers (see [what an MCP server is](https://www.pluginstackai.com/start-here/)).

- **Cost:** free. **Certificate:** certificate of completion.
- **Link:** [Introduction to Model Context Protocol](https://anthropic.skilljar.com/introduction-to-model-context-protocol)

### Hugging Face Agents Course

A free course that takes you from beginner to building your own AI agents, using frameworks like smolagents, LlamaIndex and LangGraph, and ending with a final project. You need basic Python, a free Hugging Face account and an internet connection.

- **Cost:** free.
- **Certificate:** follow along for free in "audit mode", or do the assignments to earn one of its two certificates.
- **Link:** [Hugging Face Agents Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/agents-course/unit0/introduction)

### Hugging Face LLM Course

How large language models work and how to use, fine-tune and share them with the Hugging Face libraries. It needs a good knowledge of Python, and Hugging Face suggests taking an intro deep learning course first (such as fast.ai below).

- **Cost:** completely free, with no ads.
- **Certificate:** the course FAQ says there isn't a certification for it yet.
- **Link:** [Hugging Face LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1)

### fast.ai: Practical Deep Learning for Coders

A free course for people with some coding experience (about a year, ideally in Python) and high-school math. There are 9 lessons of about 90 minutes each, and the book it's based on is free online too. You use free tools for building and running models.

- **Cost:** free.
- **Link:** [course.fast.ai](https://course.fast.ai/)

### Harvard CS50's Introduction to AI with Python

Harvard's course on the ideas and algorithms behind modern AI: search, knowledge, uncertainty, optimization, machine learning, neural networks and language. It's seven weeks of lectures and projects. You need CS50x or at least a year of Python.

- **Cost:** free through Harvard's OpenCourseWare.
- **Certificate:** score at least 70% on each project for a free CS50 Certificate. A verified certificate from edX costs extra.
- **Link:** [cs50.harvard.edu/ai](https://cs50.harvard.edu/ai/)

## FAQ

### Which free AI course is best for a complete beginner?

Elements of AI if you want to understand AI in general, or Claude 101 or OpenAI Academy if you want to get better at using an AI assistant. None of them need coding.

### Do free courses give you a certificate?

Some do. Anthropic Academy and the Hugging Face Agents Course offer free certificates, OpenAI Academy gives badges, and CS50 AI has a free CS50 Certificate. DeepLearning.AI certificates need a paid membership.

### I finished a course. What next?

Try it for real. Our [Start here](https://www.pluginstackai.com/start-here/) page walks you through installing Cursor or Claude Code and adding your first MCP server. Then browse the [directory](https://www.pluginstackai.com/) for tools to add.
